sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Distribution of Excess Multilayer Ceramic Capacitors and Resistors

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Marshall Islands (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - U.S.-derived common law statutory corporate framework (Business Corporations Act modeled on the Delaware General Corporation Law) with Marshallese customary law limited to land-holding matters
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association between the Republic of the Marshall Islands and the United States of America (1986, amended 2003) - economic, trade and investment provisions
US-RMI Intergovernmental Agreement (IGA) for FATCA and tax information exchange (2015)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus) - trade agreement with Australia and New Zealand (in force for RMI)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: RMI Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2018 (AMLCFTA), as amended, administered by the Marshall Islands Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU); RMI Business Corporations Act 1990 (BCA), as amended through the 2021-2022 transparency reforms (maintenance of registers of directors, shareholders and beneficial owners and production of such records to the Registrar of Corporations upon lawful demand); Registrar of Corporations Beneficial Ownership Reporting Rules and FIU Customer Due Diligence Guidelines; FATF Recommendation 24 and APG Mutual Evaluation follow-up commitments.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each director, shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport office or notary public of the holder's country of citizenship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing state is a Convention member; otherwise consular legalization by the RMI or a recognized foreign consular authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address and source of funds declaration for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank, licensed utility provider or independent notary in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter covering the UBO's full transaction history and reputational standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank maintaining the UBO's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: RMI Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: RMI Ministry of Foreign Affairs apostille (if required by an opening bank or counterparty)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation and Certificate of Incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: RMI Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: RMI Ministry of Foreign Affairs apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the RMI registered agent and law firm
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of execution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every director, shareholder, UBO, signatory and counterparty principal against: (i) the RMI FIU advisory list and domestic adverse-information and PEP indicators under AMLCFTA; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List and any RMI-designated sanctions; (iii) OFAC's SDN and non-SDN consolidated screening, contractually required by U.S.-dollar correspondent banks; and (iv) international enforcement databases including World Bank sanctions, INTERPOL notices and regulatory disqualification lists. PEPs and high-risk profiles require enhanced due diligence with independent corroboration of source of wealth and source of funds, escalation to the compliance officer, and continuous transaction monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Marshall Islands Corporate Registry - Office of the Registrar of Corporations (Majuro); name reservation filings are lodged through licensed resident Registered Agents under the BCA.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must appear on the public record in Roman/Latin script. Marshallese and English are the official languages; a foreign-script name (e.g., Chinese, Cyrillic or Arabic characters) must be accompanied by a transliterated Roman-alphabet form, and the transliterated form is the operative registered denomination. Names must be distinguishable upon the record within the meaning of the BCA; a suffix such as 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited' or 'Ltd.' does not itself create distinguishability.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: any word implying connection with the RMI Government or a foreign government, or any word contrary to public policy or public morals
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, the applicant, through its licensed registered agent, files a written Request for Reconsideration with the Registrar of Corporations in Majuro within 21 business days, attaching evidence of distinguishability and, where applicable, the prior written consent of the holder of a similar name. The Registrar must issue a reasoned determination within 15 working days. A second rejection may be appealed to the High Court of the Marshall Islands as an administrative review; an applicant may also re-file a fresh name reservation after the obstacle is removed or the conflicting name is withdrawn.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Fully permissible for a non-resident passive business corporation. The BCA requires a continuous registered office and a resident Registered Agent in the Republic, but the registered office may be the physical address of the licensed agent; no local employees, premises, stock or operational facilities are required for a tax-exempt non-resident BC.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 5-7% probability of an unannounced physical inspection during the first year of operation for a low-risk, non-resident, passive electronics distribution entity with no physical local footprint; the probability rises to roughly 15-20% upon the introduction of PEP ownership, irregular wire activity, or adverse media and screening hits.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate name search and reservation fee (initial 60-day reservation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RMI Office of the Registrar of Corporations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per Registrar of Corporations fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RMI Office of the Registrar of Corporations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing tariff (fee varies with authorized capital; USD 300 benchmark for standard structure)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent and registered office service - first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed RMI resident registered agent (corporate services provider)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for RMI registered agent service

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation Anti-Money Laundering and CFT due diligence, UBO piercing, PEP and sanctions screening file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance officer of the licensed corporate services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; AMLCFTA CDD obligations passed through by the service provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariffs plus prevailing apostille and consular fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for offshore corporate formation legal fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Issuing licensed commercial bank / professional referee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: International courier, administrative expediting and certified-copy dispatch

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act 1986 (as amended), codified as Title 27 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code (27 MIRC), especially Sections 12 (Articles of Incorporation), 13 (Effect of Filing), 14 (Bylaws), 15 (Registered Office and Registered Agent), 16 (Issue of Shares) and 56 (Board of Directors).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Majuro (registry administered through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade; submissions are effected exclusively through licensed RMI registered agents).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (duplicate original bearing notarized incorporator signatures and the registered agent's written consent), with a Certificate of Incorporation issued upon registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement; the Board fixes the stated capital and par value at its discretion, and shares may be issued for such consideration as the Board approves.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Bylaws submitted to this first meeting be, and hereby are, adopted as the Bylaws of the Corporation. RESOLVED, that the subscription agreement for the issuance of 1,000 common shares, par value US$0.01 per share, is ratified; the Secretary is directed to record the subscriber in the share register. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation be fixed at the office of the licensed registered agent, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the registered agent is appointed. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, to serve until successors are elected. RESOLVED, that the President is authorized to open bank accounts, execute documents, and pay all incorporation expenses and fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations (name clearance channel) via a licensed RMI registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two or three proposed corporate names in writing. The Registrar applies the distinctiveness test and will reject names likely to mislead or to conflict with existing registered entities. Reserve the approved name pending the filing of the Articles of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate names in order of preference
Engagement letter appointing the licensed registered agent
Passport copies of the proposed directors and incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the preferred name is refused or conflicts with an existing entity, select a fallback name or file an alternative; alternatively, obtain a written letter of no-objection from the existing name holder and re-submit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, execution and notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator(s) acting privately; notarization before a notary public or a Marshall Islands consular official
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles in accordance with 27 MIRC Section 12, stating the corporate name, authorized share capital and par value, the initial directors, the registered office location and the appointed registered agent. Have each incorporator sign and acknowledge the instrument; obtain the registered agent's signed consent to act.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation
Notarized signature pages of the incorporators
Written consent of the registered agent to act
Statement of authorized shares and par value
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notarization is defective, re-execute before a competent notary; if the Articles omit a mandatory clause, amend the draft and re-notarize before filing to avoid rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation and payment of government fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Majuro (lodged by the licensed registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the duplicate original Articles together with the registered agent's consent and the US$200 filing fee through the appointed registered agent. The Registrar examines the instrument for compliance with the Business Corporations Act and endorses the date of filing upon acceptance.
required_dossiers: Duplicate original Articles of Incorporation
Registered agent consent
Government filing fee receipt (US$200)
Name reservation certificate (if issued)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar returns a rejection notice, cure the stated defect within 30 days by amendment and re-submission with a fresh fee; if the defect is non-substantive, file a certificate of correction rather than a new registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and creation of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon acceptance, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation, upon which corporate existence commences (27 MIRC Section 13). Confirm that the registered office reflects a physical street address in Majuro maintained by the registered agent and that the agent's details are recorded in the public register.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Filed duplicate of the Articles of Incorporation
Registered agent confirmation of the office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains a clerical error, request a Certificate of Correction from the Registrar; if the registered agent resigns, file a change of agent within 30 days to avoid administrative default.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational action: Bylaws, first board resolution, share issuance and officer appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial Board of Directors (private corporate records; no registry filing required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The initial directors adopt the Bylaws and the First Board Resolution, approve the share subscription agreement, issue share certificates, and appoint the President, Secretary and Treasurer. The Secretary opens the corporate minute book and share register and records the registered office resolution.
required_dossiers: Bylaws
First Board Resolution (minutes)
Share subscription agreement and share certificates
Register of members and register of directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the share consideration is disputed, the Board re-approves the issuance at par and records a correcting resolution; if an officer declines office, the Board appoints a replacement by written consent in lieu of a meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration administrative compliance: good standing, tax status and banking
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations; RMI Tax and Revenue Office; selected commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Certificate of Good Standing and confirm the non-resident entity's tax status with the RMI Tax and Revenue Office (no business privilege tax is levied on non-resident corporations deriving no RMI-source income). Open the corporate bank account and file the annual administrative return to preserve good standing.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Bylaws
Board resolution opening bank accounts and designating signatories
Director and officer identification and proof of address
Certificate of Good Standing and registrar's tax status letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a notice of default for unpaid annual fees, pay the arrears and late penalties within 30 days to avoid dissolution; if the corporation is administratively dissolved, apply for reinstatement under the Business Corporations Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — non-resident Business Corporation conducting passive wholesale distribution (ISIC 4652); no manufacturing or industrial establishment is based in the Republic of the Marshall Islands. If a physical warehouse is later opened in Majuro, a Business License would be required from the RMI Tax and Revenue Office under the Business License Act.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no industrial operating licence or manufacturing permit is required for the distribution of multilayer ceramic capacitors and resistors. Any future import activity would be subject to an RMI Customs import declaration under the Customs Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI EPA), established under the Environmental Protection Act 1984 (40 MIRC Ch. 1)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA — the passive storage and distribution of electronic components is not a prescribed activity requiring an Environmental Impact Assessment; a general registration with RMI EPA is triggered only if the operations include manufacturing, waste treatment or fuel storage.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process emissions, wastewater discharge or VOC thresholds apply to this activity. If warehousing is established, the operator must prevent uncontrolled solid-waste disposal, comply with RMI EPA standards for stormwater and municipal waste, and handle any end-of-life electronic inventory in accordance with the Basel Convention transboundary movement rules applicable to the Marshall Islands.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for a virtual non-resident entity. If a physical office or warehouse is later opened in Majuro, the lessee must obtain a building occupancy clearance from the Majuro building inspector, a fire-safety certificate from the RMI Fire and Rescue Service, and, for any staff, an occupational workplace registration under the RMI occupational health and safety regime.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) — Ministry of Finance, Banking and Postal Services, Revenue and Taxation Division (Majuro, Delap), jointly with the Registrar of Corporations of the Office of the Attorney General for entity registration. RMI operates no centralized national electronic tax-filing portal; registrations are submitted in paper form to the Revenue and Taxation Division or through licensed registered agents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Because the RMI does not impose a corporate income tax, VAT, or sales tax on a non-resident offshore Business Corporation, no statutory TIN or VAT registration number is issued to such an entity. The de facto tax identifiers are: (1) the certificate of incorporation and corporate registration number issued by the Registrar of Corporations under the Business Corporations Act; (2) the annual Business License number issued by the Ministry of Finance under the Business License Act (the license number functions as the primary taxpayer identifier); and (3) the RMI Customs importer code where goods are imported into or exported from the RMI. The foreign-entity procurement sequence is: (i) incorporate a Business Corporation with a registered agent and registered office in Majuro; (ii) obtain a Foreign Investment Business License under the Foreign Investment Act (unless the activity falls within the reserved domestic-investor schedule); (iii) obtain the annual Business License; (iv) register with the RMI Customs Division for an importer/exporter code if any physical goods movement through RMI customs occurs; and (v) if a local payroll is ever created, register with the RMI Social Security Administration as an employer. A Non-Resident Domestic Corporation declaration may additionally be filed with the Revenue and Taxation Division to formally evidence non-liability for RMI-source income tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — an RMI-incorporated Business Corporation with non-resident ownership and no income derived from sources within the RMI (i.e., passive electronic component distribution conducted entirely offshore) falls outside the RMI income tax net. The RMI applies a strict territorial/offshore model: no corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, no withholding tax, and no estate or gift tax on such entities. Only income derived from sources within the RMI would be taxable under the Income Tax Act 1989, which is generally inoperative for offshore non-resident domestic corporations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: RMI law contains no US-style check-the-box election and no hybrid-mismatch (BEPS Action 2) election. The available statutory mechanisms are: (a) Non-Resident Domestic Corporation status — a domestic corporation wholly without RMI-source income may formally elect/declare exemption from the RMI income tax under the Income Tax Act 1989; (b) entity-form elections under the RMI Limited Liability Company Act and Limited Partnership Act — an RMI LLC or LP may be treated as a partnership or disregarded entity for foreign tax purposes (e.g., US federal Form 8832 check-the-box classification), whereas an RMI Business Corporation is treated as a per se corporation; and (c) no treaty or hybrid-entity election is available because the RMI maintains no comprehensive double-taxation agreement network.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None — the RMI does not levy a national VAT, GST, or sales-and-use tax. Indirect taxation is limited to customs import duties under the Customs Tariff Act (as amended) and selective excise duties on fuel, alcohol, tobacco, and certain luxury goods, which apply only at importation into the RMI.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: N/A — there is no turnover-based threshold triggering VAT/GST registration because no value-added or sales tax exists. Any person carrying on business in the RMI, including a foreign-owned distributor, must instead obtain an annual Business License regardless of revenue; license fees depend on the business classification, not turnover. Importers must additionally register with the RMI Customs Division and obtain a USD-denominated importer code; no de minimis tax-registration threshold applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No electronic-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) mandate exists under RMI law. Commercial invoices are not cleared or stamped by any tax authority. Customs import and export entries are lodged with the RMI Customs Division through licensed customs brokers using paper or basic electronic filing; documentary records must be retained for customs audit, but no national e-invoicing repository or government clearance platform applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable in VAT terms — because the RMI has no VAT system, there is no 0% export VAT rate to claim and no input-VAT refund mechanism. Under the Customs Tariff Act, goods exported from the RMI (including re-export of imported passive electronic components such as multilayer ceramic capacitors and resistors) are generally free of export duty. Import duty paid at the time of importation may be reclaimed through the customs drawback/remission mechanism where the goods are physically re-exported without having been sold, consumed, or domestically disposed of in the RMI, provided the exporter substantiates the identity of the goods and the fact of export within the statutory claim period.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Entry / Export Declaration (RMI Customs form lodged by a licensed customs broker)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from the RMI
Original Import Entry and duty-paid receipt (required for duty-drawback or re-export claims)
Commercial Invoice and packing list identifying the MLCC/resistor part numbers, quantities, and tariff classifications
Certificate of Origin or evidence of final foreign destination (as requested by counterparty banks)
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT credit advice evidencing collection of export proceeds from the overseas buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export fraud in the RMI takes the form of customs drawback abuse rather than VAT zero-rating fraud, given the absence of VAT. Under the Customs Tariff Act (as amended), false drawback declarations, over-invoicing of re-exported goods, misdescription of tariff classifications, smuggling, or diversion of 'exported' goods back into the RMI market attract retrospective clawback of the duty refunded, monetary penalties of up to three times the duty involved, forfeiture of the goods or conveying vessels, fines of up to USD 10,000, and imprisonment of up to five years for individuals involved. The Revenue and Taxation Division and the Attorney General's office may jointly audit exporter records for up to five years, and a non-compliant exporter's Business License may be suspended or revoked.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No domestic central bank exists in the Marshall Islands. The de facto monetary authority is the U.S. Federal Reserve System because the U.S. dollar is the sole legal tender. Domestic bank licensing and prudential supervision are undertaken by the Banking Commissioner within the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of the Marshall Islands.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The U.S. dollar is fully convertible with no exchange controls or quantitative limits. Both capital account and current account transactions are unrestricted. Profit remittance and dividend distributions by a non-resident Business Corporation require only a valid board resolution and standard solvency tests under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act. No foreign exchange approval, surrender obligation, or non-resident withholding tax applies to such outbound payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender or conversion requirement. Exporters may retain 100% of USD-denominated export receipts in any authorized account, onshore or offshore, with no time limit. The mandatory conversion ratio is 0% (zero) for all export proceeds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD Account with segregated Capital Escrow sub-ledger

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High as a supplementary payment rail only. The Republic of the Marshall Islands has no standalone licensing regime for electronic money institutions, and the Banking Act 1989 prohibits unauthorized deposit-taking. Offshore EMIs may act as payment facilitators or digital currency custodians, but they do not replace the need for a physical licensed bank account. Legal constraints require that all USD clearing ultimately settle through a U.S. correspondent bank. EMIs operating in RMI territory without a banking license are not permitted to accept deposits from the public.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For onshore licensed banks (Bank of Marshall Islands and Bank of Guam RMI Branch), directors and authorized signatories must normally appear physically at the branch in Majuro for original signature verification and a KYC interview. Remote opening is generally not permitted by domestic RMI banks. Offshore international correspondent banks may accept a notarized and apostilled remote opening package if the entity is non-resident, but the RMI Banking Commission cannot compel any bank to extend such service.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived high-risk offshore jurisdiction with minimal economic substance; foreign shareholders and no public beneficial ownership register.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of good standing from the RMI Registrar of Corporations; board minutes demonstrating active commercial management; audited financial statements; entity chart with ultimate beneficial owners; signed UBO declarations with passport copies and proof of residential address; professional reference letters from licensed introducers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction profile inconsistency for a passive electronic inventory distributor, including high wire frequency without supporting trade documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed commercial contracts with suppliers and customers; purchase orders; invoices; bills of lading; customs declarations; warehouse inventory reports; shipping insurance certificates; and monthly trade reconciliation statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee shareholder structures, bearer instruments, or inability to attribute funds to a verified natural-person beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Banks-required beneficial ownership form; passport and address notarizations; source of wealth declarations; source of funds credentials; notarized nominee declaration and trust deeds (if any); independent bank reference letters from the remitting institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of U.S. dollar clearing with counterparties domiciled in high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening policy; restricted-party certification; corporate trade compliance manual; counterparty risk assessment; transactional flowcharts proving arms-length dealings with low-risk suppliers and customers; sub-certifications from each trading partner.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital injection is routed via SWIFT MT103 from the beneficial owner's source account to the RMI Business Corporation's operational account. The wire should reference the company registration number and field 70 must state 'EQUITY SUBSCRIPTION - CAPITAL INJECTION'. A board resolution authorizing the capital contribution must be chartered and retained. For amounts exceeding USD 50,000, the bank will request source-of-funds documentation, including recent bank statements, wealth evidence, and the underlying subscription agreement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade supplier payments are executed via SWIFT MT103 with field 70 specifying 'TRADE PAYMENT - INV [invoice reference]'. For large-value or documentary trade transactions, irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 may be opened and confirmed by a U.S. or Asian correspondent bank. Recurring inventory purchases may be settled via open-account ledger with monthly net settlement through CHIPS or Fedwire. The Marshall Islands has no domestic clearing house; all USD clearing is ultimately processed through U.S. correspondent banks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/CNH deliverable forwards executed under ISDA with a licensed international bank counterparty
USD/JPY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for hedging JPY-denominated supplier liabilities
Cross-currency swaps (USD versus CNY or JPY) for long-term balance sheet hedging
Capped option collars on major trade currencies to protect margins while preserving upside

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report (Form AR): current directors, officers, registered office, principal office, authorized capital and share schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands (Ministry of Finance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary month of certificate of incorporation plus the immediately following calendar month (2-month filing window)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty: 10% of the annual report fee for each month or part thereof, capped at 100% of the fee; company ceases to be in good standing; Certificate of Good Standing withheld; administrative strike-off after two consecutive years of non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Declaration (annual UBO confirmation and shareholder-transfer updates)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Office of the Registrar of Corporations, RMI Beneficial Ownership Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the Annual Report (within 2 months of anniversary); each change in beneficial ownership reported within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty up to US$1,500 per violation; loss of good standing; no Certificate of Good Standing; possible administrative strike-off; individual liability of officers for wilful non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None for a non-resident Business Corporation under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act; no statutory audit, review, or public filing of financial statements for passive trading/distribution entities. Mandatory audit applies only to licensed financial institutions and entities so ordered by a court.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No statutory accounting standard mandated by the Business Corporations Act; IFRS is the market-standard framework when financial statements are voluntarily prepared; statutory record-keeping duty under BCA Section 57.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Beneficial Ownership Act 2018 (as amended) requires the registered agent to hold current UBO records; the Annual Report form contains the UBO confirmation schedule; every share transfer or change in a 10%-or-greater beneficial interest must be reported to the Registrar within 30 days, including transfers of passive electronic distribution inventory assets.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders' and Directors' Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required by statute; voluntary IFRS audit, if lender- or shareholder-required: US$5,000 - US$12,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (non-resident Business Corporation exemption; RMI nominal corporate rate of 3% applies only to income derived from sources within the Marshall Islands and is not triggered)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Non-resident Business Corporation is outside the RMI income tax net. No corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, no branch profits tax, no payroll tax for non-resident staff, and no withholding tax on dividends, interest, or royalties. Annual government fee and registered agent fee are the only recurring costs; no economic substance fee applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: None for income tax. Annual Report to the RMI Registrar of Corporations, filed by the licensed registered agent via the RMI corporate registry system or physical submission; no income tax return form is prescribed for non-resident exempt corporations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Annual Report and annual government fee must be submitted on or before the end of the calendar month containing the anniversary of incorporation, not the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Entity name and certificate number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full registered corporate name and Business Corporations Act incorporation number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name appearing on the Certificate of Incorporation; do not use trade names or abbreviated variants.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Registered agent and registered office
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and address of the Marshall Islands licensed registered agent and the registered office street address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the agent's licensed RMI address; the non-resident company itself may not claim a street address in the RMI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names and usual residential addresses of all directors and officers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident individuals are permitted; include foreign residential addresses and confirm no RMI residency requirement applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names and addresses of shareholders and beneficial owners required under RMI AML/beneficial ownership reporting.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: 100% non-resident ownership is allowed; report beneficial owners accurately to the registered agent; bearer shares are prohibited for exempt companies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Principal activity and asset location
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Brief statement of business purpose and physical location of principal assets and operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State 'distribution of electronic components outside the RMI' and confirm no RMI premises, inventory, employees, or business conduct.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Officer or director certification that the corporation has not derived RMI-source income and has not conducted business within the RMI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Sign only if accurate; engaging in RMI business or deriving RMI-source income invalidates the exempt non-resident status.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: No late income tax return penalty exists because no income tax return is due. Late submission of the Annual Report triggers Registrar late fees and collection of the unpaid annual government fee, with administrative dissolution or striking-off if the delinquency continues; reinstatement requires payment of arrears, penalties, and reinstatement fees.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - no Marshall Islands dividend withholding tax on distributions to non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No DTA relief procedure is required because RMI imposes no source-based withholding tax. For foreign fiscal authorities that require proof of non-resident tax status, the registered agent may obtain a tax status attestation from the RMI Registrar based on the exempt BC classification; this is not a treaty relief application. RMI has no comprehensive double tax treaty network.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory withholding on outbound interest and IP royalties; no treaty rates apply. Inbound US-source royalties or interest may be subject to 30% US withholding because no US-RMI comprehensive income tax treaty exists.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 0 - no statutory RMI Local File or Master File obligation. As defensive practice, prepare OECD-aligned transfer pricing documentation and an intercompany distribution policy when controlled transactions exceed USD 10,000,000 or when a foreign parent jurisdiction imposes a lower threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: RMI does not maintain Economic Substance Regulations comparable to BVI or Cayman. However, under foreign CFC, substance-over-form, and permanent establishment doctrines, the passive electronics inventory business must be owned, managed, and administered with real operational substance in the foreign operating jurisdiction; maintaining a pure RMI shell is a fatal compliance red flag.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the RMI non-resident BC as a shell to conceal sales income of a foreign operating business, backdating invoices, or interposing the entity without commercial substance to evade home-country corporate tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: RMI does not tax the entity, but the beneficial owner's home jurisdiction may impose tax reassessments, interest, civil fraud penalties up to 100% of the tax due, criminal fines, and asset seizure; RMI may terminate corporate registration if fraudulent filings are proven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false certificates or participate in sham transactions can be personally liable for civil restitution; criminal tax evasion convictions carry imprisonment of up to 5 to 10 years and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining no real bank account, no operational oversight, nominee directors with no control, unreported beneficial owners, or failing to keep accounting records for the passive component distribution business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the RMI Business Corporations Act and AML regime, the Registrar may strike off or dissolve the company; foreign courts may disregard the entity and attribute its income to the beneficial owner; banks terminate wire and credit facilities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers face personal liability for trading while dissolved, fines for failure to maintain records, disqualification orders, and criminal liability if nominee arrangements facilitate money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering / Beneficial Ownership Reporting Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify beneficial owners, failing to report them to the registered agent, or processing Swift wire payments from unknown counterparties without adequate AML/KYC checks on the electronics distribution transaction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: RMI AML/CFT regulations impose administrative fines per violation, regulatory suspension or revocation of the registered agent, potential criminal fines, and striking-off of the corporate entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers can be prosecuted individually for money laundering facilitation; penalties include imprisonment, personal fines, confiscation of proceeds, and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing multilayer ceramic capacitors or resistors with military or dual-use functionality to embargoed or sanctioned end users, or processing payments through a sanctioned bank using Swift wires.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: US Export Administration Regulations and OFAC sanctions apply extraterritorially even when routed through RMI; maximum criminal penalties include USD 1,000,000 per violation and debarment from export privileges; RMI may impose licensing sanctions on imports and exports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors who order or knowingly benefit from prohibited exports may be criminally liable, fined personally, imprisoned for up to 20 years under US law, and placed on denied-party lists or travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Declaration to Registrar / Fraudulent Incorporation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting false beneficial ownership data, forged director consents, or a false non-resident declaration while actually carrying on business in the RMI or deriving RMI-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the RMI Business Corporations Act, the Registrar may require dissolution, impose monetary penalties, and refer the matter to the Attorney General; the company loses its tax-exempt status and becomes liable for any RMI gross revenue or business licensing tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and incorporators who sign false declarations are jointly and severally liable for resulting RMI fees, taxes, penalties, and third-party losses; courts may impose imprisonment and travel bans.
